title: Caesar Salad
subtitle: Cos lettuce with proper anchovy dressing and Parmesan
excerpt: Cos lettuce dressed in a creamy anchovy and Parmesan dressing, topped with garlic croutons and plenty of grated Parmesan. The classic Caesar dressing is made from scratch in a bowl, not from a jar.

recipe.sourceNotes: Caesar salad was created by Caesar Cardini, an Italian immigrant restaurateur, at his restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico in 1924. The original dressing used whole egg, Worcestershire sauce, anchovy fillets, lemon juice, and Parmesan. Over time the raw egg has been replaced with pasteurised egg or mayonnaise in many home versions. This recipe uses the traditional method with a whole egg emulsified with anchovy and Parmesan for the closest result to the original.

recipeTools.notes: For making and tossing the dressing.

content.text: The dressing must be made in the bowl: the Parmesan and anchovy are pounded directly into the base of the bowl with the back of a spoon or a fork, then the egg yolk and lemon juice are whisked in before the olive oil. Dress the leaves at the last moment so they stay crisp.

items.preparation: outer leaves removed, inner leaves torn
half finely grated for dressing, half shaved to serve
thick-cut, torn into rough chunks for croutons

content.text: Make the croutons: toss the bread chunks with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and a crushed garlic clove. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6 for 10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.

In a large salad bowl, mash the anchovy fillets with the back of a fork until they become a paste. Add the remaining crushed garlic clove and mash together. Add the egg yolk, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and Dijon mustard. Whisk to combine.
Whisk in the remaining olive oil in a slow, steady stream until the dressing is creamy. Stir in the finely grated Parmesan. Season with black pepper.
Add the cos lettuce leaves to the bowl and toss to coat every leaf. Add the croutons. Scatter the shaved Parmesan over the top. Serve immediately.
